Job Description
Surface Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) Operators employ electronic receivers and associated analysis and recording equipment in the collection of
Radio Detection and Ranging (RADAR), and other signals within the electromagnetic (EM) spectrum; interpret intercepted electronic signals to de-
termine their source to support the tactical Common Operational Picture (COP); execute tactics in accordance with doctrine; and report information
to tactical and strategic commanders in support of Fleet, Theater, and National requirements.

Cryptologic Technicians (Technical) (CTT) conduct Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) in support of National and Commander’s tasking; operate and maintain electronic sensors and computer systems; collect, analyze, exploit, and disseminate Electronic Intelligence (ELINT) in accordance with National and Fleet tasking; provide safety of forces, Indications and Warning (I&W), Information Operations (IO), and Anti-Ship Missile Defense (ASMD); and provide technical and tactical guidance to Warfare Commanders and National consumers in support of surface, subsurface, air, information, strike, and special warfare operations. __________________________________________

Surface Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) Operators employ electronic receivers and associated analysis and recording equipment in the collection of Radio Detection and Ranging (RADAR), and other signals within the electromagnetic (EM) spectrum; interpret intercepted electronic signals to de- termine their source to support the tactical Common Operational Picture (COP); execute tactics in accordance with doctrine; and report information to tactical and strategic commanders in support of Fleet, Theater, and National requirements.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
